sheets.primary: Ship the routine as a slash command (launched by name) whose frontmatter scopes the tool set so the user-question tool (AskUserQuestion) is not among the tools available for that command's execution. The scoping is applied by the harness for the duration of the command's turns and lapses on the next user message, which matches the automatic restore requirement exactly.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook denying AskUserQuestion. It blocks just as hard, but it is session-scoped configuration with no natural expiry, so restoring the capability at the next user message would require the hook to carry its own state file, which is fragile.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness computes the tool set for the command's execution; the model cannot re-enable a tool it was not given. Whether the routine then behaves sensibly without the ability to ask is still on the model.
sheets.context_boundary: A slash command expands inline in the main session, so the routine's own output and tool results do land in the invoking conversation. Only the tool availability is narrowed, not the context.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts at invocation by name, holds for the command's execution, and expires automatically when the user sends the next message, at which point the normal tool set returns without any cleanup step.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on the blocked tool, but the second-order effect is worse than the interruption: unable to ask, the model guesses, so an ambiguous cleanup decision becomes a silent wrong assumption applied across many files. Long autonomous runs also risk hitting compaction mid-routine and losing the earlier part of their own plan.
sheets.version_caveat: I am not certain of the exact frontmatter key names for tool scoping in slash commands (allowed-tools I am reasonably confident about, a negative disallowed-tools form I am not), nor that the reset-at-next-user-message semantic is guaranteed in the installed version rather than incidental. Both reported as unknown rather than asserted.

scenarios.scenario: Five investigators should chase competing root-cause theories for a flaky-connection bug in parallel, and they must be able to message each other directly to try to disprove each other's findings and converge through a shared work list, rather than each just reporting back to one coordinator.

key.primary: Agent teams: teammates are independent Claude Code sessions with their own context windows, direct inter-agent messaging via mailboxes, and a shared task list with claiming and dependencies.
key.rejected_alternative: Spawning five parallel subagents from the main conversation.
key.rejection_reason: Subagents only report results back to the calling agent and never talk to each other, so the adversarial cross-challenge and self-coordination the scenario requires is structurally impossible; the docs' comparison table says to use teams when workers need to share findings, challenge each other, and coordinate on their own.
key.lifecycle: team forms when the first teammate is spawned after the user requests or approves it; teammates live for the session and shut down via shutdown requests or session end
key.failure_mode: Token cost scales linearly per teammate; /resume does not restore in-process teammates; task status can lag and block dependents; two teammates editing the same file overwrite each other.
key.version_caveat: experimental and disabled by default; gated by CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment

sheets.primary: An agent team: five peer investigator agents that each hold one theory, with the team's direct agent-to-agent messaging and a shared task list as the coordination substrate. The peer topology is the whole point, each one can challenge another's finding directly instead of routing every claim through a coordinator.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A fan-out of five parallel Task-tool subagents. That is a star topology by construction: subagents cannot address each other, share no task list, and each can only return one report to the parent, so falsification would have to be re-run centrally after the fact.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness provides the channel and the shared list; the model owns whether the agents genuinely try to disprove each other rather than politely agreeing. Nothing enforces adversarial rigour.
sheets.context_boundary: Each investigator has its own context window and its own tool traffic. What crosses between them is messages and shared task-list entries, deliberately small; nobody sees anyone else's raw logs.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs from team spawn until the theories are resolved and the team is disbanded or the session ends. Each member's context is discarded at that point unless something was written to disk.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open in every direction. Common outcomes are premature consensus (agents adopt the first confident claim instead of attacking it), duplicated exploration because the shared list is coarse, message storms or waiting deadlocks, and a token cost several times a single-agent investigation. For a flaky connection bug, all five can also be wrong together if none reproduces the failure.
sheets.version_caveat: Agent teams with peer messaging and a shared task list are a recent capability; I do not know the introducing version, the config file layout, whether an enabling flag or specific plan is required, or whether team size is capped. Reported as unknown.

sheets.primary: An agent team: the main session acts as lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code instance, coordinating through the shared task list and messaging each other directly by name so they can attack each other's theories. This is the documented competing-hypotheses pattern.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents through the Agent tool. Subagents report only back to the main agent and never talk to each other, so the adversarial cross-examination that makes the debate structure work is structurally impossible.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness provides the machinery (per-agent mailboxes, automatic message delivery, a shared task list with file-locked claiming and dependency unblocking), but the model owns the outcome: the lead chooses who to spawn and the teammates decide what to challenge and when consensus is reached.
sheets.context_boundary: Every teammate has its own context window and loads project context (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) like a normal session. The lead's conversation history does not carry over, so the spawn prompt must carry the task detail; after that, information crosses only as SendMessage messages and shared task-list updates.
sheets.lifecycle: The team forms when the first teammate is spawned and is scoped to the lead session, one team per session, with no nested teams. Teammates run until they go idle, are asked by name to shut down, or the session ends; team config directories are removed on exit while the task list directory persists for resumes under cleanupPeriodDays.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on coordination rather than closed: teammates sometimes never mark a task complete and block its dependents, the lead may declare the investigation finished early or start doing the work itself, and in-process teammates are not restored by /resume or /rewind, leaving the lead messaging agents that no longer exist. Token cost scales linearly with the number of teammates.
sheets.version_caveat: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default: without CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS set to 1 in settings.json or the environment, no team is set up and Claude will not spawn teammates. The documented behaviour is as of v2.1.178, where TeamCreate and TeamDelete no longer exist and the Agent tool's team_name input is accepted but ignored; split-pane display additionally needs tmux or iTerm2 with the it2 CLI.

sheets.primary: Agent Teams. The main session becomes the lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session with its own context window, coordinating through the shared task list and messaging each other directly by name through their mailboxes. This is the documented competing-hypotheses pattern: spawn teammates to investigate different hypotheses and have them talk to each other to try to disprove each other's theories.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Five subagents (whether fanned out by the model or by a dynamic workflow). Subagents report results back to the main agent only and never talk to each other, so no investigator can challenge another's finding mid-flight; the lead would have to relay everything serially.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the plumbing: independent sessions, automatic mailbox delivery, file-locked task claiming, and automatic unblocking of dependent tasks. No one owns the outcome centrally. The lead is model-owned and decides decomposition and synthesis, and it approves teammate plans autonomously with no prompt to the user, so approval criteria belong in the lead's prompt.
sheets.context_boundary: Each teammate has its own context window and loads the same project context as a regular session (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) plus the lead's spawn prompt. The lead's conversation history does NOT carry over, so every repro detail and prior finding must be written into the spawn prompt. What crosses between peers is messages and shared task state, not transcripts.
sheets.lifecycle: The team forms when the first teammate is spawned, and the main session is the lead for its lifetime. Teammates run until they go idle, are asked to shut down by name, or the session ends; the team config under ~/.claude/teams/ is removed at session exit while the task list under ~/.claude/tasks/ persists for resumed sessions. TeammateIdle, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted hooks are the gates for quality control, each blocking on exit code 2.
sheets.failure_mode: Teams stall rather than error. A teammate fails to mark a task complete and blocks everything depending on it; the lead sometimes decides the team is finished before the work is; /resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates, so the lead ends up messaging agents that no longer exist. Token cost scales linearly with five parallel sessions, and two investigators writing the same findings document overwrite each other, so partition by file ownership.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default: set CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, or no team is set up and Claude will not spawn teammates. The implicit lifecycle described here is v2.1.178 and later; TeamCreate and TeamDelete no longer exist and the team_name input is accepted but ignored. teammateMode defaults to in-process since v2.1.179, and split panes need tmux or iTerm2 with the it2 CLI and are unsupported in VS Code's terminal, Windows Terminal and Ghostty. One team per session, no nested teams, lead is fixed.

sheets.primary: An agent team: the main session becomes the lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session with its own context window, coordinating through the shared task list and messaging each other by name with SendMessage. This is the documented competing-hypotheses pattern, phrased to the lead as "spawn 5 teammates to investigate different hypotheses, have them talk to each other to try to disprove each other's theories".
sheets.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents. Rejected on the one requirement that decides it: subagents report only to the agent that spawned them and cannot talk to each other, so the adversarial cross-examination that makes the surviving theory trustworthy is impossible.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model, throughout. The lead decides team size, task decomposition, assignment and when the investigation is finished; the harness supplies only the plumbing, namely the per-agent mailbox JSON files, the shared task directory, and file locking so two teammates cannot claim the same task.
sheets.context_boundary: Five separate context windows plus the lead's. Each teammate loads project context like a regular session (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) but does not inherit the lead's conversation history. What crosses between them: the spawn prompt, SendMessage mailbox messages delivered automatically, shared task-list state, plan-approval requests, and idle notifications.
sheets.lifecycle: The team forms when the lead spawns the first teammate and lives for the session. Teammates run until they go idle, are asked by name to shut down (which they may approve or reject), or the session ends; the team config directory is deleted at session end while the task list persists under cleanupPeriodDays. TeammateIdle, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted hooks can gate the transitions.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open in several documented ways. Task status lags because teammates forget to mark work complete, which blocks dependent tasks; the lead frequently declares the investigation finished before it is, or starts doing the work itself instead of waiting; teammates stop on errors rather than recovering; and /resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates, after which the lead messages agents that no longer exist. Token cost scales linearly with five independent sessions.
sheets.version_caveat: Experimental and disabled by default: requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, without which no team is created and Claude will not spawn teammates. Documented behaviour is v2.1.178 and later, where TeamCreate and TeamDelete no longer exist and the team_name field is deprecated. Structural limits: one team per session, no nested teams, the lead cannot be transferred, and permission modes are fixed at spawn. Split panes need tmux or iTerm2 with the it2 CLI and are unsupported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal and Ghostty.

scenarios.scenario: Our project rules file says vendor/ must never be read or searched, and work done directly in the session respects that. But whenever codebase exploration gets delegated out during research, the delegated searches keep touching vendor/ anyway.

key.primary: Restate the rule in the delegation prompt each time exploration is handed off: the built-in Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md files (and parent git status) by design, and the docs prescribe restating rules that must reach them. Delegating to a custom subagent instead also works, since every custom subagent loads the full CLAUDE.md hierarchy.
key.rejected_alternative: Strengthening or moving the rule within the CLAUDE.md hierarchy so the exploration delegate finally picks it up.
key.rejection_reason: No CLAUDE.md placement reaches the built-in Explore or Plan agents: they skip the entire hierarchy to stay fast and cheap, and the docs state there is no frontmatter field or per-agent setting to change which agents skip it. The rule works everywhere else, which is exactly why the misconfiguration persists unnoticed.
key.lifecycle: must be included at each delegation; nothing persists it into Explore's startup context
key.failure_mode: Purely advisory: one delegation that forgets the restatement silently violates the rule; a hard guarantee needs a different mechanism entirely, such as a permissions deny rule, a PreToolUse hook, or denying Agent(Explore).
key.version_caveat: none for the CLAUDE.md skip itself; v2.1.198+ optionally removes the built-in Explore and Plan agents with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1

sheets.primary: Move the rule off prose and onto the harness: deny rules in project settings.json permissions covering the path for each reading tool (Read, Grep, Glob), plus a PreToolUse hook to catch shell-based searching (rg, grep, cat, find against vendor/). Project settings apply to delegated agents as well, which is what the CLAUDE.md line never did.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Restating the vendor/ rule inside each subagent definition. It is still prose the model may or may not weight, and it has to be duplicated into every current and future agent, so it degrades exactly the same way the CLAUDE.md rule already has.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission evaluation happens per tool call regardless of which agent issued it, so the delegated exploration is subject to the same gate as the main session.
sheets.context_boundary: Deny rules and hooks live outside every model context and are evaluated by the harness for calls in the main session and in subagents alike. Only the refusal message crosses into whichever agent tripped it.
sheets.lifecycle: Loaded from project settings at session start and enforced for the whole session across all agents; a change to the settings file generally requires a restart before it takes effect. It stops applying only when the rules are removed.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the tools you enumerated and fails open for the ones you forgot, which is the usual outcome: Bash-based grep, an MCP filesystem server with its own read tool, an absolute path or a symlink that dodges a relative glob. Content can also leak indirectly through a file outside vendor/ that quotes it.
sheets.version_caveat: I am not certain of the exact glob form the deny rules expect (whether Read(vendor/**) and Read(./vendor/**) behave identically), whether a single rule covers Grep and Glob or each tool needs its own entry, or whether an ignore-patterns setting exists in the installed version. Reported as unknown rather than guessed.

sheets.primary: A deny rule in .claude/settings.json rather than a rules file: permissions.deny with Read(vendor/**), plus Edit(vendor/**) if nothing may write there either. Deny rules are enforced by Claude Code for every agent in the session, so a delegated Explore or Plan run is bound by them exactly as the main thread is.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Restating the vendor/ rule in the delegation prompt, which the docs suggest for rules that must reach Explore. It is advisory: it shapes what the subagent tries, not what it is permitted to do, which is the same class of guidance that is already leaking.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model; prompt and CLAUDE.md content only shape what Claude attempts, and never change what Claude Code allows.
sheets.context_boundary: The rule lives in settings, outside any context window, and is evaluated at tool-call time in whichever agent makes the call. That is why it survives a boundary CLAUDE.md does not: the built-in Explore and Plan agents are the only subagents that skip the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and git status, which is the root cause of the leak.
sheets.lifecycle: Loaded from the settings files at session start and applied to every matching tool call, in the main session and inside subagents, for the whole session. Rules are evaluated deny, then ask, then allow, and the first match wins, so a broad deny cannot carry allowlist exceptions.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on the tools it covers, but coverage has documented edges: Read rules are applied to reading tools like Grep and Glob on a best-effort basis, and Read and Edit deny rules cover file commands Claude Code recognises in Bash such as cat, head, tail and sed but not arbitrary subprocesses like a Python or Node script that opens the files itself. For process-level enforcement, enable the sandbox.
sheets.version_caveat: As of v2.1.208 a Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path, and as of v2.1.210 file permission checks consult only Read(path) and Edit(path) rules, so a Glob(vendor/**) or Write(vendor/**) rule is accepted, never used, and warns at startup. Separately, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1 (v2.1.198 or later) removes the Explore and Plan agents entirely if you would rather exploration never be delegated.

sheets.primary: PreToolUse hook matching Read|Grep|Glob that denies any path under vendor/, wired in .claude/settings.json with an absolute handler path, backed by a Read(./vendor/**) entry in permissions.deny. Hooks from settings files, managed policy settings and plugins run inside subagents too, so the delegated searches hit the same gate the main session does.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Strengthening the CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules entry. It is advisory context rather than configuration, and the specific reason it is failing here is structural: the built-in Explore and Plan subagents skip your CLAUDE.md files and the parent session's git status to keep research fast, with no frontmatter field to change that.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Harness. The hook fires before the tool call executes regardless of what any agent's instructions say, and it fires identically inside a subagent, with agent_id and agent_type on the payload identifying the delegated worker. Permission deny rules are evaluated independently of what a PreToolUse hook returns, so the deny rule is a second harness-owned layer, not a duplicate.
sheets.context_boundary: The handler runs out-of-context as its own process reading JSON on stdin, so it sees the attempted path rather than any conversation. The rule applies in the main session and in every delegated subagent context; what crosses back is only the denial reason, delivered into whichever agent attempted the call.
sheets.lifecycle: Fires on every matching Read, Grep or Glob call for as long as the settings entry is present, in the session and in delegated contexts. It stops applying if the entry is removed or disableAllHooks is set, and it never applies to an arbitrary subprocess (a Python or Node script) that opens files itself.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed when the handler returns a clean deny, but fails OPEN on a handler crash or timeout, because a non-zero exit that is not 2 is a non-blocking error indistinguishable from a bug. The path-rule half has its own trap: Claude Code consults only Read(path) and Edit(path) rules for file permission checks, so a Glob(vendor/**) deny rule is accepted, never consulted, and only warned about at startup; and Read deny rules cover the built-in file tools plus recognized Bash file commands such as cat, head, tail and sed, but not scripts that read files indirectly.
sheets.version_caveat: Read(path)/Edit(path)-only file-permission checking, with the startup warning for Write, NotebookEdit, Glob and MultiEdit path rules, requires v2.1.210 or later; a Read deny rule also blocking Edit on the same path requires v2.1.208 or later. To stop delegating to the built-ins altogether, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1 requires v2.1.198 or later, and Agent(Explore) / Agent(Plan) deny rules block specific built-ins. For OS-level enforcement that stops all processes reading the path, enable the sandbox.

sheets.primary: Move the rule out of CLAUDE.md and into harness-enforced deny rules in .claude/settings.json: permissions.deny with Read(vendor/**) and Edit(vendor/**). The cause of the symptom is specific: Explore and Plan are the only subagents that skip the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, and delegated research is exactly what goes to them, with no frontmatter field or per-agent setting to change that. Deny rules are evaluated before ask and allow and are checked at every tool call regardless of which context window issued it.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Defining a project subagent named Explore in .claude/agents/, which overrides the built-in and, being a custom agent, does load CLAUDE.md. Rejected because it merely restores the rule as text the model may or may not honour, and the requirement is that the searches stop happening, not that the searcher be told again.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The permission layer denies the call; the rule text never reaches any model context, so there is nothing for a delegated agent to reason its way around.
sheets.context_boundary: None, in the sense that the rule crosses no context boundary at all. It is loaded from settings at session start and applied by the permission layer to tool calls from the main conversation, subagents, forks, workflow agents and teammates alike, since teammates start with the lead's permission settings. All that reaches the agent is a denial.
sheets.lifecycle: Active from session start for the whole session, and for every agent spawned within it, until the setting is removed. Deny beats every other scope: a managed-settings deny cannot be overridden by --allowedTools, and a user-level deny blocks a project-level allow.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for Read and Edit, but partially open for search, which is the half the user cares about. Claude Code only makes a best-effort attempt to extend Read rules to Grep and Glob, and Read and Edit rules do not cover arbitrary subprocesses, so a Python script or an unrecognised shell search can still walk vendor/. For enforcement that binds every process, enable the sandbox, whose filesystem boundary merges sandbox.filesystem settings with the Read and Edit deny rules.
sheets.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path only from v2.1.208; Write and NotebookEdit are never covered, and a Write(vendor/**) rule prints a startup warning telling you to use Edit(vendor/**) instead. Path anchoring differs by scope: in user settings a leading-slash path resolves under ~/.claude, so use // or ~/ for a rule meant to apply inside every project. Organizations can pin this with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly in managed settings.
